briefings.title: The Enron-Era Tricks Are Back in AI: How These Companies Are Hiding Their Debt | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Steve Eisman warns that high interest rates and AI-driven off-balance-sheet financing techniques—reminiscent of Enron and the Global Financial Crisis—are returning in full force.

briefings.title: The Big Short Partners Reunite: Rates, AI, Gold and Two Stock Picks | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 75
briefings.tldr: Steve Eisman reunites with former Big Short partners Vincent Daniel and Porter Collins to discuss macroeconomic pressures, the mechanics of modern hedge fund shorting, and the bull/bear cases for AI, gold, and alternative asset plays.

briefings.title: Is OpenAI the Achilles’ Heel of the US Economy? | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: The U.S. economy's heavy reliance on massive AI capital expenditures—which account for roughly half of projected 2026 GDP growth—makes it vulnerable, with OpenAI acting as a critical Achilles' heel whose potential failure could trigger an immediate recession.

briefings.title: AI’s Achilles’ Heel: Why Everything Hinges on Anthropic & OpenAI | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Steve Eisman examines the structural risks in the AI boom—highlighting hyperscalers' heavy reliance on Anthropic and OpenAI—while analyzing market uncertainty, the dynamics between entrenched businesses and upstarts, and the declining appeal of Bitcoin.

briefings.title: The Q2 2026 Report Card: Who Won, Who Lost, and Why | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: While Q2 2026 saw strong overall gains for the S&P 500 (+13%) and Nasdaq (+18%), a critical market shift occurred as investors fled capital-intensive tech "hyperscalers" lacking competitive moats in favor of scarce hardware plays like Micron, while software and consulting sectors suffered severe AI-driven disruption.

briefings.title: Earnings Keep the Market Strong Despite Signs of Consumer Weakness | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: The U.S. economy remains bifurcated ("K-shaped"), where massive AI-driven infrastructure spending by Big Tech and industrials continues to propel the market upward despite clear evidence of a recession among low-to-middle-income consumers.

briefings.title: Iran War Volatility, Private Credit Fears Grow, & Solar Continues to Crash | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: Market volatility is currently driven by the escalation of war in Iran and a rapidly deteriorating narrative in private credit, where rising fraud, redemption "gating," and sudden devaluations suggest the first significant credit cycle since 2008.

briefings.title: Flight to Safety Begins, Private Credit Cracks & the Software Bloodbath Continues | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: The market is shifting from performance chasing to a flight to safety, evidenced by a 20% collapse in software and a surge in consumer staples.

briefings.title: AI Panic Spreads, Health Insurers Crack & Retail Keeps Buying | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: The market is currently characterized by a "shoot first, ask questions later" mentality as AI-driven panic spreads from software into sectors like insurance and logistics, while structural failures in health insurance models and a struggling low-end consumer suggest underlying economic fragility.

briefings.title: Lakshmi Ganapathi on Consumer Stress & the Cracks Beneath the US Economy | The Real Eisman Playbook
briefings.tldr: The US economy is experiencing a "silent recession" and a "vibesession" where headline credit data remains stable only because of "extend and pretend" lender tactics and Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) acting as a hidden bridge for overleveraged consumers.
